terms.comment: A description of ours. We have found no term for baking a pastry case empty in Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini, and no ancient recipe that does it: Cato builds his placenta whole and bakes it once (Cato Agr. 76). Solum is Cato’s word for the base (see “base”, of a cake or tart). For the beans that weigh the paper down, fabīs onerāre; see the examples.
Pliny’s word for boiling a thing beforehand; solum praecoquere is ours.

phrases.latin: Solum prius ināne coquēmus; deinde impēnsam īnfundēmus.
phrases.english: We’ll bake the base empty first; then we’ll pour in the filling.

phrases.latin: Chartam super solum pōne et fabīs onerā, nē intumēscat.
phrases.english: Put paper over the base and weigh it down with beans, so that it doesn’t puff up.

sources: Lewis & Short: solum · Lewis & Short: inanis · Lewis & Short: praecoquo · Lewis & Short: faba
